newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch say Zaire force must disarm Rwandan refugees.
newsitem.headline: Dutch say Zaire force must disarm Rwandan refugees.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said on Thursday the international force to be sent to aid starving Rwandan refugees in Zaire should be mandated to repatriate them and disarm those among them who bore weapons.
"In our view it would be by far the best if the mandate created the possibility of sending the people back to Rwanda, not just creating a safe corridor," he told Dutch television.
"In our view that would require disarming the armed forces among the refugees and that is a big problem because opinion is divided on this," he added.
Van Mierlo said the Dutch might have to decline to take part in the humanitarian operation in Zaire if its conditions for the mandate were not met, but said he hoped this could avoided.
The position outlined by the Dutch minister is at odds with that of some of the bigger countries expected to contribute to the Canadian-led force which could number more than 10,000 men.
The United States, Britain and France have made clear that it should only safeguard relief supplies and not attempt to disarm the powerful Hutu militia established in eastern Zaire.
But aid officials and diplomats say that if they are not disarmed it will be impossible to distribute food, water and medicine properly to the more than one million refugees.

Hundreds of thousands of Hutus poured into eastern Zaire in 1994, fearing reprisals by victorious Tutsi rebels for a campaign of genocide launched by the Hutu-led army and militia groups, but supported by large sections of the population.

Many refugee camps were run by the same Hutu killers, many local mayors and regional leaders, who then used them as bases from which to launch a comeback, infuriating the new Tutsi-led government in the Rwandan capital Kigali.

The Netherlands has been preparing 270 members of its Air Mobile Brigade for duty in Zaire but has not yet taken a decision to send them. The cabinet is expected to discuss the issue at its regular weekly meeting on Friday.
